drivingQuestion: What degree of impurity does R' Akiva's case involve?
outcomeNote: sets up the redundancy difficulty that opens the next unit

segments.he: הוֹסִיף רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא: מִימֵיהֶן שֶׁל כֹּהֲנִים לֹא נִמְנְעוּ מִלְּהַדְלִיק כּוּ׳. מִכְּדֵי שֶׁמֶן שֶׁנִּפְסַל בִּטְבוּל יוֹם מַאי הָוֵי — שְׁלִישִׁי. וְכִי מַדְלֵיק לֵיהּ בְּנֵר שֶׁנִּטְמָא בִּטְמֵא מֵת מַאי הָוֵי — שֵׁנִי.
segments.en: It was stated in the mishna that «Rabbi Akiva added: In» all «the days of the priests, they did not refrain from lighting» teruma oil that was ritually disqualified by coming into contact with one who immersed himself during that day, in a lamp that was rendered ritually impure with first-degree impurity through contact with one who became ritually impure with impurity imparted by a corpse. The Gemara asks: «Now» consider, «what is» the status of «oil that was disqualified by one who immersed himself during that day?» As one who immersed himself during that day assumes second-degree impurity, the oil that he touches assumes «third-»degree ritual impurity status. «And when he lights it in a lamp that was rendered ritually impure through» contact with one who became «ritually impure» with impurity imparted by «a corpse,» who has first-degree impurity status, «what is» the impurity status of the oil? It assumes «second-»degree ritual impurity status.

moves.about: computes the degrees: the oil is third-degree and becomes second-degree

edges.about: computes the degrees: the oil is third-degree and becomes second-degree

positions.claim: the oil goes from third to second degree
positions.basis: tevul yom is second; corpse-impure lamp is first
